newsitem.title: CHINA: China June RPI up 0.8 pct yr/yr-China news service.
newsitem.headline: China June RPI up 0.8 pct yr/yr-China news service.

text.p: China's retail price inflation rose by 0.8 percent year-on-year in June, the China news service said on Thursday.
That was the same as the increase of 0.8 percent for May and compared with 1.1 percent in April and 1.7 percent in March.
The report said retail price inflation for the first half would be below 2.0 percent but gave no specific figure.
It forecast benchmark retail price inflation for the whole year to be around 3.0-4.0 percent, compared with an official target of 6.0 percent and down from 6.1 percent last year.
It cited several major factors in the cooling of inflation, including the steady fall in food prices. Food prices rose by just 1.3 percent in the first half, it said.

Since April, food prices had shown negative growth, with prices on the grain market now lower than state-set purchasing prices, it said. This marked a significant turnaround from a few years ago when food prices were the major factor in skyrocketing inflation, it said.

In the first five months, prices of industrial consumer goods inched up 2.6 percent year-on-year, while prices of household electrical appliances, telecommunications equipments, garment, shoes, hats and jewelry have been falling since the beginning of the year, it said.
Housing prices jumped 10.2 percent in the first five months compared with the year-ago period, it said.
